# Every permission the release APK may ask for, as Exodus's scanner reads it from the merged manifest.
# exodus-scan.sh fails a build whose APK asks for anything not listed here, or no longer asks for
# something that is: a permission can't arrive (or leave) unnoticed through a library's manifest.
# A permission the app declares itself is also explained to the user in the app.

# Declared by the app (AndroidManifest.xml).
# Approximate location, once when an outing starts, to find its county (#27). Explained on the page before
# Android's prompt (app/src/main/java/io/cosgriff/flywaybracket/ui/home/LocationExplain.kt).
android.permission.ACCESS_COARSE_LOCATION
# INTERNET (install-time; the user is never asked): the league server, the only host the app talks to
# (ADR 0001, #38). Nothing is sent before the player agrees on the consent page that League and Bracket
# show first; README.md, Privacy, says what.
android.permission.INTERNET
# ACCESS_NETWORK_STATE (install-time; the user is never asked): whether the connection is metered, so that
# a pack download over 5 MB asks first on mobile data (#39). Only that yes or no is read. README.md,
# Privacy, says so.
android.permission.ACCESS_NETWORK_STATE

# Merged in from libraries. Install-time; the user is never asked for it.
# androidx.core, which protects the app's own unexported receivers with it:
io.cosgriff.flywaybracket.DYNAMIC_RECEIVER_NOT_EXPORTED_PERMISSION
